result.vpp_package_detail: After Xvfb install (sudo apt-get install xvfb), v++ -p -t hw_emu --package.boot_mode=qspi PASS in 2m22s. Produced BOOT.BIN + launch_hw_emu.sh + qemu QSPI flash images. No host.elf was passed (XRT SDK not installed; cannot build host).
result.hw_emu_qemu_boot_detail: launch_hw_emu.sh boots qemu-system-aarch64 + Xilinx PMC simulator. qemu reaches u-boot prompt (Versal>) on the PMC-driven QSPI image. PLM, ATF, u-boot all load cleanly.
result.hw_emu_userspace_block_reason: u-boot's default boot.scr tries to load image.ub (PetaLinux FIT) from mmc/usb/jtag or via TFTP. None exist on the QSPI image. TFTP from 10.0.2.2 returns 'Access violation' (no TFTP server in the qemu host network). Result: qemu sits at the u-boot prompt indefinitely with no userspace to run the host app that would drive the AIE graph.
result.host_elf_block_reason: XRT SDK is not installed on the ECS host. host.cpp uses #include <experimental/xrt_kernel.h>, <experimental/xrt_aie.h>, <adf/adf_api/XRTConfig.h>; XILINX_XRT env var is empty; find / -name xrt_kernel.h finds nothing. Without XRT headers + libxrt_coreutil/libxrt_core, the host.cpp cannot be compiled to host.elf, and even if compiled it would need a PetaLinux rootfs with libxrt at runtime.
result.petalinux_image_block_reason: Building a PetaLinux image.ub for VCK190 requires the PetaLinux tool (not just Vitis), a kernel BSP for the v++ link XSA, and ~30-60 min of build time per iteration. PetaLinux is not installed on the ECS host (no /tools/Xilinx/PetaLinux/). The base_platform xilinx_vck190_base_202410_1/sw/ ships boot.scr + u-boot + bl31 + system.dtb but NO Image/rootfs — the user is expected to build those with PetaLinux.
result.aie_latency_us_measured_block_reason_cha: (1) Xvfb missing → FIXED after sudo apt-get install xvfb. (2) v++ -p succeeded. (3) qemu boots to u-boot. (4) No PetaLinux image to boot Linux. (5) No XRT SDK to build host.elf. (6) AIE driver call cannot be issued from u-boot directly — needs userspace with XRT runtime.

key_finding: Xvfb fix unblocked v++ -p and qemu boot. The next hard blocker is the missing PetaLinux+XRT software stack on the ECS host — required to RUN a userspace app that drives the AIE graph and reads the cycle counter. This is a host-admin task (install PetaLinux tool + build Image+rootfs+XRT for the v4 platform) outside autonomous worker scope. T0042 analytic 160 us remains the published AIE latency.
options_for_orch: (A) HOST-ADMIN: install PetaLinux 2024.1, build VCK190 base BSP with XRT + AIE drivers, rebuild xpfm to include sw/sysroots + Image; then worker rebuilds host.elf, repackages, and runs hw_emu to measurement. Estimated 1-3 days human time + auto runtime.

(B) BAREMETAL ALTERNATIVE: skip PetaLinux entirely; write a baremetal C++ app using AIE_DRIVER (Xilinx's bare-driver API in /tools/Xilinx/Vitis/2024.1/aietools/...) and build via standaloneBSP. The baremetal app reads aiecompiler-generated cycle counters directly without Linux/XRT. ~1 day worker time.

(C) DEFER: keep T0042 analytic 160 us as published with [AIE-SCHED-EST] honesty label. The chess-backend HW compile PASS + x86sim bit-exact + tile profile already validate the design architecturally. hw_emu measurement becomes a camera-ready item or post-paper follow-up.

(D) ON-BOARD: physical VCK190 board with PetaLinux SD card and XRT installed; the only path to a real silicon-thermal-correct measurement. Multi-week procurement + setup; clearly out of scope for the FCCM submission.
